title: hyperbilling-mcp docs
nav.label: Sections
hero.title: HyperBilling over MCP
hero.body: A Model Context Protocol server that exposes the Megazone HyperBilling Open API as read-only tools. One tool call is one HyperBilling request, with nothing cached or rewritten in between.
arch.title: Architecture
arch.direct.hint: An agent connects straight to this server.
arch.litellm.hint: A LiteLLM proxy sits in front as the MCP gateway.
flow.label: Architecture: an AI agent calls hyperbilling-mcp over MCP, and the server sends one HTTPS request to the HyperBilling Open API and returns its answer.
flow.agent.detail: kagent, Claude, or any MCP client
flow.step1: The agent picks a tool and calls it with its arguments.
flow.step2: The server forwards the caller's credential headers.
flow.step3: HyperBilling returns the billing rows as JSON.
flow.step4: The agent answers the cost question from those rows.
connect.title: Connect
connect.body: The server speaks streamable HTTP at /mcp on this host. Point an MCP client at it and send your HyperBilling credentials as headers.
connect.prompt.body: Or let the agent set itself up. Copy this prompt, paste it into an MCP client such as Claude Code, and replace the email with your HyperBilling login. The URL is the address this page was opened at.
connect.prompt:
Register the hyperbilling MCP server in my user-scope MCP configuration.

- Name: hyperbilling
- Transport: HTTP (streamable HTTP)
- URL: {{origin}}/mcp
- Header X-Client-Id: user@example.com
- Header X-Client-Secret: ${HYPERBILLING_API_KEY}

Keep ${HYPERBILLING_API_KEY} as an environment variable reference. Do not ask for the key and do not write its value anywhere.
Then call hyperbilling_list_linked_accounts to confirm the connection.
connect.start: Start with hyperbilling_list_linked_accounts. Every other tool takes the account IDs it returns.
litellm.title: Through LiteLLM
litellm.body: Register this server on a LiteLLM proxy to give every model and client behind the proxy the same billing tools, with LiteLLM handling keys, access control, and usage logs.
litellm.label: Architecture with LiteLLM: clients call the LiteLLM proxy, which calls hyperbilling-mcp over MCP, which sends one HTTPS request to the HyperBilling Open API.
litellm.clients.detail: Anything that holds a LiteLLM key
litellm.config: Add the server to the LiteLLM config.yaml. The http transport is streamable HTTP.
litellm.endpoint: Clients then connect to /hyperbilling/mcp on the proxy, or to /mcp/ for every server at once. LiteLLM prefixes each tool with the server name, so the search tool becomes hyperbilling-hyperbilling_search_billing.
litellm.credentials: For credentials, either configure the fallback credential on this server and send nothing from LiteLLM, or let each caller send its own as x-mcp-hyperbilling-x-client-id and x-mcp-hyperbilling-x-client-secret, which LiteLLM forwards as the two HyperBilling headers.
auth.title: Authentication
auth.body: HyperBilling authenticates each request with two headers. The server forwards the pair a caller sends, so a caller sees only the linked accounts its own key can read.
auth.client_id: The HyperBilling login email that issued the key.
auth.client_secret: The Open API key from the HyperBilling console. It expires one year after it is issued.
auth.fallback: A caller that sends neither header uses the fallback credential when the operator configured one. Without a fallback the call is refused before it reaches HyperBilling.
limits.title: Limits
limits.body: These are HyperBilling limits. The server passes them through unchanged.
errors.title: Errors
errors.body: A request HyperBilling rejects comes back as a tool error that carries the API message, so the agent can correct the call. Only a request that got no response fails the MCP call itself.
errors.204: No billing data matches the query. Returned as a normal, empty result.
errors.400: A required field is missing, a value is malformed, or a limit was exceeded.
errors.401: A header is missing, the key expired, the client ID does not own the key, or a linked account in the request is not readable with the key. The API body is dropped because it echoes the key.
errors.403: Authenticated, but no linked account is visible to this client ID.
errors.404: The API has no such request path.
errors.429: The hourly request limit was exceeded. Retry later.
errors.500: The API failed on its side. Retry later.
endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.readyz: Readiness. 503 until the HyperBilling API has been reached once, 200 from then on.
endpoints.metrics: Prometheus metrics for tool calls, tool latency, and API requests.
tools.title: Tools
tools.body: Generated from the tool definitions this server registers, so it always matches what tools/list returns.

api.title: HyperBilling Open API
api.hero: Reference for the Megazone HyperBilling Open API, written from the official guide and checked against the live API. The official guide remains the source of truth.
api.base.title: Base URL and headers
api.base.body: Every request goes to this host over HTTPS.
api.base.key: A key is bound to the account that issued it. Sent with another account's email, it is rejected with 401.
api.linkedaccount.body: Lists the AWS linked accounts the credentials can read. Every other request takes these account IDs.
api.tag.body: Lists the cost allocation tag keys of each linked account. LinkedAccount sits at the top level here, not under Filter.
api.billing.body: Returns billing rows for a period, grouped by up to five dimensions.
api.recent.body: Fixed reports. The path sets the period and the grouping, and the body carries only the linked accounts.
api.field.granularity: MONTHLY for a period of up to 24 months, or DAILY for up to 31 days.
api.field.time_period: Start and End, the first and last day of the period as YYYY-MM-DD.
api.field.region: Optional. Keeps only these regions, as AWS usage report abbreviations such as APN2 for Seoul.
api.field.service_code: Optional. Keeps only these AWS service codes such as AmazonEC2.
api.field.next_data_token: Optional. The NextDataToken of the previous response, to fetch the next page.
api.filter.unknown: The API silently ignores a Filter key it does not know, so an unfiltered result means the key was wrong.
api.view.last_3_months: Monthly totals of the last three months, current month included.
api.view.last_6_months: Monthly totals of the last six months, current month included.
api.view.latest_from_last_month_daily: The month ending at the newest billing date, by day.
api.view.latest_by_product: Current month by AWS service code.
api.view.typo: The lastest spelling in one path is the API's own.
api.values.title: Values
api.response.title: Response format
api.response.body: Both billing requests answer in one format.
api.resp.group_by: The value of each dimension. USAGE_DATE is YYYY-MM for a monthly query and YYYY-MM-DD for a daily one. A value is null when the row has none, such as an untagged resource.
api.resp.value: The requested measures as numbers. A cost can be negative.
api.resp.token: Empty on the last page. Otherwise send it back as Filter.NextDataToken for the next 1000 rows.
api.status.title: Status codes
api.status.204: No billing data matches the query. The body is empty.
api.status.401: A header is missing, the key expired, the client ID does not own the key, or a linked account in the request is not readable with the key. The response body echoes the submitted key, so keep it out of logs.
api.status.403: Authenticated, but no linked account is visible to this client ID. Not reproduced here, since a linked account the key cannot read answered 401.
api.source.detail: MegazoneCloud's own reference and the source of truth for this page.
api.endpoints.body: All {{count}} requests of the official guide. Every one only reads data.
api.summary.billing: Billing rows for a custom period, grouping, and measures.
api.summary.tag: Cost allocation tag keys of each linked account.
api.summary.linkedaccount: Linked accounts the credentials can read.
api.summary.estimated: Estimated cost of the current month.
api.estimated.body: Estimates the cost of the current month from the daily cost trend. Amounts are in USD and dates are in UTC. It answers 400 while the month has too little data.
api.est.current: Total cost from the first day of the month to latestBillingDate.
api.est.estimated: Estimated cost of the whole month, a linear regression over the daily costs.
api.est.last_month: Total cost of the previous month.
api.est.change: Change from the previous month in percent, (EstimatedCost - LastMonthCost) / LastMonthCost × 100, to two decimal places.
api.est.six_months: Month and Cost of the last six months, current month included.
api.est.latest_date: Last usage date in the billing data, YYYY-MM-DD. That day can be partial and its amount can still change.
api.field.filter: The fields under Filter fields below.
api.field.group_by: One to five of the dimensions under Values.
api.field.result: One or more of the measures under Values.
api.filter.title: Filter fields
api.filter.body: Fields of Filter in /v1/search/billing. Each array keeps the rows that match one of its values.
api.field.use_billing_period: true selects rows by billing period start date instead of usage date. A daily query then covers the month of TimePeriod.Start.
api.field.tag: Key is a tag key and Values an optional list of its values. Without Values, every row that carries the key matches.
api.field.match: Keeps only rows with one of these values.
api.field.one_of: One or more of these values.
api.field.reservation_option: One or more of these values, as the guide lists them. None of them matched live rows whose payment option is All Upfront, so the spelling the API accepts is unconfirmed.
api.dim.region: Region, as an abbreviation from the table below.
api.dim.lineitem_type: Line item type, such as Usage, Discount, or Support.
api.dim.reserved_purchase_type: Reserved Instance payment option, such as All Upfront.
api.dim.reserved_account: Account that owns the Reserved Instance.
api.dim.savings_plans_account: Account that owns the Savings Plan.
api.dim.tag: A tag key from /v1/search/tag after TAG:, for example TAG:user:Team.
api.status.400: A required field is missing, a value is malformed, a limit was exceeded, or the month has too little data for an estimate.
api.status.404: The request path does not exist.
api.status.500: Server error. The guide also lists a missing required field here, but the live API answers 400 for it.
api.error.body: An error answers with this JSON body.
api.limit.end: TimePeriod.End cannot be later than the current month.
api.regions.title: Region abbreviations
api.regions.body: Values of Filter.Region and of the REGION dimension, as AWS usage reports abbreviate them. Charges without a region come back as Global.
api.regions.name: Region
